scores_applied.fc_derivation: Stage 3 factual_accuracy_score, as returned (reflects pre-correction errors found; not re-inflated)

changes.from: ...down from 18.3% in 2019, and coverage read it as relief.
changes.to: ...down from 18.3% in 2019. In the same survey, the share of adults overweight or obese rose again to 54.4%...
changes.reason: Stage 3 UNVERIFIED: no primary source shows coverage/headlines framed it as relief. Removed the media-characterisation claim; the headline carries the 'looks like relief' framing instead.

changes.from: ...and headlines called it the epidemic easing.
changes.to: ...and the drop looks like good news.
changes.reason: Stage 3 UNVERIFIED_DETAIL: 'headlines called it the epidemic easing' has no source. Reframed as the reader's likely interpretation, not an asserted media fact.

changes.from: ...The number that sets tomorrow's diabetes moved the other way.
changes.to: ...The risk factor that drives future diabetes moved the opposite way.
changes.reason: Stage 3 MISLEADING: 'the number that sets tomorrow's diabetes' is too strong/causal. Softened to 'risk factor that drives', which the sources support.

changes.from: More than one in two adults, about 11 million people, now carry excess weight, the strongest driver of type 2 diabetes.
changes.to: More than one in two adults now carry excess weight, a major modifiable driver of type 2 diabetes.
changes.reason: Both stages flagged '11 million' as unverified/inconsistent (Stage 2 math: ~12.5M; Stage 3: secondary media only). Dropped the figure rather than substitute an extrapolation. 'strongest driver' -> 'a major modifiable driver' per Stage 3 OVERCLAIM (WHO/NIDDK list several risk factors).

changes.from: ...Among those aged 18 to 29, about 84% are unaware.
changes.to: ...Among those aged 18 to 29 with diabetes, about 84% are unaware.
changes.reason: Stage 3 denominator fix: 84% is of 18-29-year-olds WHO HAVE diabetes, not all 18-29s.

changes.from: The headline rate counts the diagnosed. The real burden hides in the undiagnosed, and it skews young.
changes.to: The 15.6% already includes people a survey blood test caught unaware, not only those formally diagnosed.
changes.reason: Stage 3 INCORRECT (m_false 0.87): the 15.6% is NOT diagnosed-only; it is known diabetes 9.7% + survey-detected raised blood glucose 5.9%. Rewrote to state this accurately. Also removed 'skews young' (Stage 3 MISLEADING: prevalence rises with age; only unawareness skews young, already covered in big).

changes.from: Physical inactivity is the modifiable input feeding the weight curve, and it sits upstream of every clinic visit.
changes.to: Physical inactivity is a modifiable risk factor that feeds the rising weight trend.
changes.reason: Stage 3 MISLEADING: 'every clinic visit' is unsupported/overbroad. Removed; kept the supported risk-factor point.

changes.from: Diabetes is the lagging indicator. Body weight is the leading one, and it has risen at every survey since 2011.
changes.to: One year's diabetes figure is a snapshot. Body weight, a major modifiable driver, has risen at every survey since 2011.
changes.reason: Stage 3 rated leading/lagging as analytical framing (m_true 0.65). Replaced technical leading/lagging language with plainer, defensible wording; 'major modifiable driver' aligns with the corrected fact-1 claim.

changes.from: ...The waterline that decides the next decade...
changes.reason: Stage 3: 'decides the next decade' overclaims; 'shapes future risk' is supported. Analogy accepted as editorial framing (m_true 0.78).

changes.from: A health system can lower a diabetes number for a year. It cannot outrun a population that grows heavier at every survey.
changes.to: One better year in the diabetes data does not reverse a decade of getting heavier.
changes.reason: Both stages flagged the original as causal/deterministic (Stage 2 MISLEADING_FRAMING; Stage 3 OVERCLAIM: implies the system caused the dip). Rewrote to a non-causal kicker that states only what the data shows. Passes WhatsApp + subtraction test.

rejected_flags.flag: Gemini omission/evasion: 'does not explain why diabetes fell'
rejected_flags.reason: Per the T4A Accuracy Standard and confirmed by Stage 3 (claim verified, m_true 0.82: keep the omission), no primary source establishes a cause for the 2019->2023 fall. Introducing a cause would be the exact overclaim the standard forbids. The issue deliberately makes no causal claim.

residual_notes: fc held at 76 (not re-inflated) to reflect that real errors existed at review time. The errors are now corrected; a re-run would likely score higher, but the recorded stage score is the one returned.
Primary IKU PDFs (fact sheet + key findings) were opened and cited by Stage 3, satisfying the manual primary-source confirmation step for the NHMS figures used.
Issue remains published:false pending explicit publish instruction (PHASE 8 of the playbook).
